beaker.definition: A flatbottomed jar made of glass or plastic.

flask.definition: A laboratory container with a relatively narrow neck used to hold, mix, or handle material.

test-tube.definition: A slender glass or plastic container holds, combines, or warms small liquid samples in laboratory experiments.

pipette.definition: Measuring instrument consisting of a graduated glass tube used to measure or transfer precise volumes of a liquid by drawing the liquid up into the tube.
pipette.exampleUsage: The researcher selected a calibrated pipette for transferring the specified liquid volume.

graduated-cylinder.definition: A narrow glass or plastic container has numbered marks for measuring liquid volume with reasonable accuracy.

petri-dish.definition: A petri dish is a laboratory instrument used to grow microorganisms in a controlled environment.
petri-dish.exampleUsage: The researcher placed the prepared culture in a Petri dish under the approved protocol.

funnel.definition: A conically shaped utensil having a narrow tube at the small end.

burette.definition: Measuring instrument consisting of a graduated glass tube with a tap at the bottom.
burette.exampleUsage: The researcher recorded the burette’s initial reading before the approved measurement.

erlenmeyer-flask.definition: A laboratory flask with a flat base, sloping sides, and a narrow neck.
erlenmeyer-flask.exampleUsage: The guide identified the Erlenmeyer flask by its sloping sides and narrow neck.

volumetric-flask.definition: A laboratory flask marked to hold one precise volume of liquid.
volumetric-flask.exampleUsage: The researcher selected a volumetric flask marked for the required volume.

watch-glass.definition: Used in laboratories, a watch glass is a shallow dish for evaporating liquids or covering a beaker.

dropper.definition: Pipet consisting of a small tube with a vacuum bulb at one end for drawing liquid in and releasing it a drop at a time.

microscope.definition: Magnifier of the image of small objects.

bunsen-burner.definition: A Bunsen burner is a laboratory instrument used to heat and vaporize substances.
bunsen-burner.exampleUsage: The guide identified the Bunsen burner as professional laboratory heating equipment.

centrifuge.definition: An apparatus that uses centrifugal force to separate particles from a suspension.

hot-plate.definition: A flat electric surface used to heat laboratory containers.

scale.definition: A laboratory weighing instrument used to measure the mass of a sample.
scale.exampleUsage: The technician weighed the sample on the laboratory scale.

thermometer.exampleUsage: The thermometer showed the sample’s temperature.

ph-meter.definition: An instrument that measures pH, a quantity describing acidity or alkalinity in the relevant solution.
ph-meter.exampleUsage: The researcher recorded the pH meter’s reading for the specified solution.

spectrometer.definition: An instrument that measures a spectrum, such as light separated by wavelength or particles separated by mass-to-charge ratio.

incubator.definition: Apparatus consisting of a box designed to maintain a constant temperature by the use of a thermostat.

fume-hood.definition: A fume hood is a laboratory instrument used to protect workers from harmful fumes and vapors.
fume-hood.exampleUsage: The trained researcher performed the approved work in a suitable fume hood.

lab-coat.definition: Protective outerwear worn over ordinary clothes in a laboratory helps shield the wearer from spills and contaminating substances.

safety-goggles.definition: Protective glasses worn to guard the eyes.

latex-gloves.definition: Protective hand coverings made from latex; suitability depends on the hazard, material compatibility, and individual allergy risk.

face-shield.definition: A clear protective covering worn over the face to help keep droplets or splashes away from the eyes, nose, and mouth in schools, laboratories, and healthcare settings.

fire-extinguisher.definition: A portable or fixed device that releases a suitable substance to put out or contain a small fire.
fire-extinguisher.exampleUsage: The guide pointed out the fire extinguisher beside the designated exit.

eyewash-station.definition: Equipment that supplies water to rinse the eyes after an accidental exposure.
eyewash-station.exampleUsage: The guide pointed out the eyewash station during the safety briefing.

chemical-shower.definition: An emergency safety shower used to rinse hazardous chemicals from a person's body or clothing.
chemical-shower.exampleUsage: The laboratory safety tour pointed out the chemical shower.

first-aid-kit.definition: A set of supplies kept for initial assistance after an injury or sudden illness.

hazard-sign.definition: A sign that warns people about a possible danger or unsafe condition.
hazard-sign.exampleUsage: The hazard sign identified a corrosive-material area.

clamp.definition: A device used to hold laboratory equipment securely in place.

ring-stand.definition: A heavy laboratory stand with a vertical metal rod used to support clamps, rings, and equipment.
ring-stand.exampleUsage: The clamp was attached securely to the ring stand.

stirring-rod.definition: A thin rod, usually made of glass, used to stir liquids in laboratory containers.
stirring-rod.exampleUsage: The student used a clean stirring rod to mix the solution.

mortar-and-pestle.definition: A bowl and club-shaped tool used together to crush or grind solid materials.
mortar-and-pestle.exampleUsage: The sample was ground gently with a mortar and pestle.

scalpel.definition: A thin straight surgical knife used in dissection and surgery.
scalpel.exampleUsage: The guide identified a scalpel in the laboratory instrument display.

forceps.definition: A gripping instrument used to hold or handle small objects or tissues in the specified laboratory context.

syringe.definition: A device with a barrel and plunger used to draw in or dispense liquid.

magnifying-glass.definition: A handheld tool uses a curved lens to make nearby details appear larger for close viewing or reading.
magnifying-glass.exampleUsage: The magnifying glass made the small surface details easier to see.

acid.definition: In the proton-transfer model, a substance that can donate a proton in a reaction.

base.definition: In the proton-transfer model, a substance that can accept a proton in a reaction.

solution.definition: A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances.

indicator.definition: (chemistry) a substance that changes color to indicate the presence of some ion or substance.

reagent.definition: A chemical agent for use in chemical reactions.

sample.definition: A portion of material selected for examination or testing.

specimen.definition: An individual object, organism, or piece of material collected for examination.

slide.definition: A small flat piece of glass or other suitable material used to hold a specimen for microscope viewing.

stain.definition: A coloring substance used to make features of a specimen easier to distinguish.

crystal.definition: A solid whose constituent particles have a repeating ordered arrangement.

lab-notebook.definition: A book used to record experiments, observations, and results.

graph-paper.definition: Paper printed with a regular grid helps you plot data and draw graphs.

calculator.definition: A device used for doing mathematical calculations.
calculator.exampleUsage: She used a calculator to add the recorded measurements.

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.
computer.exampleUsage: The computer processed the measurements and saved the results.

data-chart.definition: An organized visual presentation of data, such as a graph or table, used to examine results.

timer.definition: A device that measures an interval or signals when a selected interval ends.
timer.exampleUsage: The timer measured the observation interval.

label.definition: A tag or marked area giving identifying information about a container or item.

barcode.definition: A set of contrasting lines and spaces allows a scanner to identify a product and access its information.

log-sheet.definition: A form or page used to record events, measurements, checks, or activities in order.
log-sheet.exampleUsage: The technician entered the temperature on the log sheet.

report.definition: A written document describing the findings of some individual or group.

autoclave.definition: Equipment using pressurized steam under specified conditions to sterilize suitable materials.
autoclave.exampleUsage: The technician checked the autoclave records for the validated sterilization cycle.

compound.definition: A substance consisting of atoms of two or more chemical elements bonded in a characteristic composition.

catalyst.definition: A substance that increases a reaction rate and is regenerated in the reaction process.

solvent.definition: A liquid substance capable of dissolving other substances.

enzyme.definition: A biological catalyst, usually a protein, that speeds a specific biochemical reaction.

analyze.definition: To make a mathematical, chemical, or grammatical analysis of.

synthesize.definition: To produce a substance by combining or reacting simpler starting materials.

calibrate.definition: To compare an instrument’s readings with a reference and establish their relationship under specified conditions.

filter.definition: To remove by passing through a filter.

extract.definition: To separate a substance or component from a mixture using a suitable method.

sterilize.definition: To eliminate viable microorganisms, including bacterial spores, through a validated process for the material.

document.definition: To record procedures, observations, or results in written or digital form.

peer-review.definition: Evaluation of research by other specialists in the same field.

apron.definition: A garment worn over clothing to protect its front during work.

tongs.definition: A tool with two arms used to grip and lift objects.

spatula.definition: A flat-ended tool used to transfer or handle material.
